_WARNING: EXPERIMENTAL PROTOTYPE. NOT AUDITED. NOT PRODUCTION. NO DEPLOYMENT. These criteria govern a measurement prototype; meeting them authorises no real value on any network.
description: THE ADMISSION BAR FOR THE GENERATION-2 ERC-20 KERNEL, PRE-REGISTERED BEFORE ANY CANDIDATE CHANGE. Every row is reconstructed from the repository's own normative sources (docs/Vault_vNext_Architecture.md, docs/Vault_vNext_Hazard_Register.md, docs/Vault_vNext_Recovery_Amendment.md, prototype/vnext-kernel/KERNEL_ADMISSION.md, prototype/vnext-kernel/AUTHORITY.md, docs/BASE_MAINNET_CUSTODY_ADJUDICATION.md) plus the owner's lane requirements, and none was written to suit the candidate. `measuredVariantA` is the classification of the candidate AS MEASURED IN PR #237 (prototype/vnext-kernel/erc20-spend-plane/contracts/VaultKernelErc20Prototype.sol), made before this lane changed anything. UNPROVEN means no Generation-2 evidence existed for the row, however much Generation-1 evidence exists: Generation-1's record is not inherited by declaration. A row may leave UNPROVEN only by naming executable Generation-2 evidence in GEN2_ADMISSION_EVIDENCE.json; test/Gen2AdmissionMatrix.test.ts refuses anything else, and refuses a row that disappears.
amendment: The rows marked addedAfterRegistration were appended after commit dbe06a68, none replacing a registered row or relaxing the residual policy. The registered rows, the description and the residual policy are unchanged: test/Gen2AdmissionMatrix.test.ts compares them with that commit.
residualPolicy: A residual is admissible only when the repository's existing policy already places its class outside the kernel's duty: a declared accepted condition (architecture section 2.2), a declared trust root (D1), a plane denial with cut 1 (section 24.2), an external asset behaviour the custody adjudication assigns to the asset boundary (custody doc sections 7.1, 8 D-5; architecture section 13.4), a sustained defect the ledger already carries with its own stated disposition (stateful/defects.ts), or a generation-publisher discovery residual (H-32). A T0 invariant that fails on a reachable state is not an admissible residual.

criteria.statement: The clone holds the admitted asset directly under the token's own ledger; there is no pool and no second number; no path removes value except an authorisation the vault's rules accept.
criteria.measuredReason: Attack tests exist (#237) but no composition campaign ran against the plane.

criteria.statement: execute is exact typed: one fixed selector on one code-bound asset, recipient and amount signed; no execute(address,bytes) surface exists anywhere.
criteria.measuredReason: Census ran only under an in-memory rename with the Generation-1 manifest; no Generation-2 manifest or call census exists.

criteria.statement: Four separate nonce domains; every signed act consumes exactly one nonce before any external effect; a refused act consumes nothing.
Every commitment written carries an exhibited preimage; rotation and recovery prove possession of the incoming credential.
Every asset-moving and credential-changing capability contains a possession test the kernel evaluates itself with ecrecover alone; with every plane removed the floor still denies.

criteria.source: KERNEL_ADMISSION K-6; architecture 4.2b and section 9; I-GUARDIAN-AUTHORITY-CLOSURE; I-GUARDIAN-CONSTITUENCY-BINDING; I-QUORUM-DISTINCTNESS; I-QUORUM-PRINCIPAL-DISTINCTNESS; I-CONSTITUENCY-RECONSTRUCTIBLE; I-GUARDIAN-FAULT-ISOLATION; I-ATTESTATION-IS-AFFIRMATIVE; I-GUARDIAN-AUTH-MODE-IS-COMMITTED
criteria.statement: The kernel is the sole writer of the commitment under a quorum of the preceding commitment; k counts distinct principals; a faulty ERC-1271 guardian changes nothing for the others.
Recovery state has one writer, liveness is the half-open window, and recovery consults only the clone's implementation, precompiles and committed guardians, never the asset and never a plane.

A quorum-approved request leaves by execution, cancellation or expiry with no principal needed for expiry; a roster replacement cannot clear it; after execution the new credential spends the admitted asset.
Both mechanisms present; the credential's veto is bounded and self-lifting; the epoch resets only on successful recovery.

criteria.source: KERNEL_ADMISSION K-10; architecture section 6; I-EXIT-REACHABILITY; I-TERMINALITY-IS-AUTHORITY
criteria.statement: Spending is NORMAL only; recovery stays live in every non-terminal state the kernel can hold a request in; migration egress stays open including from RETIRED; every state has a plane-free exit.
Containment self-expires on wall clock, cannot be extended, and holds at most 6 d in any rolling 30 d, observed from timestamps; a spend is refused while contained.

criteria.source: KERNEL_ADMISSION K-12; architecture 13.1 and 22 D2; H-10; I-MIGRATION-BINDING
criteria.statement: Binding requires quorum AND credential, fixes the destination vault and its code hash, binds no amount and no closed asset set, and can never be rebound by a caller.

criteria.source: architecture 13.2 I-MIGRATION-SUBORDINATE-TO-RECOVERY (T0) and 22 D2; H-11 Detection ('a delay-bounded warning window')
criteria.statement: For every coalition, the minimum time to complete a migration is at least the minimum time to complete a recovery, and a pending recovery blocks binding.
criteria.measuredReason: MEASURED: BIND_DELAY gates only retire(), which gates nothing; egress moves the whole balance in the bind block. On an armed floor the coalition {k guardians, ECDSA key, no PQ key} completes in 0 s against 7 d for its recovery path. The pending-recovery clause holds. Generation 1 carries the same code; no ledger entry records it.

criteria.source: KERNEL_ADMISSION K-13; architecture 13.1 and 13.2; I-MIGRATION-NONTRAP; I-EGRESS-INDEPENDENCE; I-EGRESS-RETRY-PERPETUAL; I-EGRESS-RECIPIENT-FIXED
criteria.statement: Egress is permissionless with no discretion: recipient from the binding, disposition full balance, entries independent, retry perpetual, an unsolicited or hostile asset vetoes nothing.
criteria.measuredReason: Attack tests pass. MEASURED: an issuer blocklist of the bound destination traps the admitted asset (egress refused, spending refused in MIGRATION_ONLY, no rebind). Not declared anywhere in the architecture (13.4 declares only the SOURCE case).

criteria.statement: A movement is reported only on an OBSERVED decrease of the source's own balance. A failed balance query is not an observation.
criteria.measuredReason: MEASURED: _balanceOf reads a failed query as 0. execute with amount == balance and a post-transfer query that reverts or returns short SETTLES with nothing moved and the nonce consumed; egress reports the whole balance as moved. The kernel's own comment claims this fails closed. Generation 1's egress has the same read.

criteria.source: KERNEL_ADMISSION K-14 and the SD-11 block; I-NO-CIRCULAR-ESCAPE; G-VERIFIER-ADMISSION-PROVENANCE
criteria.statement: Only a root-created verifier can become active, at all three edges; the escape from a dead or hostile verifier is guardian recovery and does not need that verifier.
criteria.measuredReason: Default test world binds the ungated fixture root.

criteria.source: KERNEL_ADMISSION K-15 and its SD5-I correction; I-NO-SILENT-DOWNGRADE-G1; I-RECOVERY-SATISFIABILITY-METADATA-INDEPENDENCE
criteria.statement: requirePq is monotone; the three metadata fields authorise nothing and cannot move an approved recovery's executability.

criteria.source: architecture 4.3 and section 11; I-PLANE-CONJUNCTIVE; AUTHORITY.md section 5
criteria.statement: A policy plane may only refuse; its call happens after the nonce and before the settlement snapshot, so it cannot influence the observation; a denying plane stops the spend and no plane reaches custody.

criteria.source: architecture 3.1, 15, 15.1; I-PURE-CONSTRUCTOR; I-CLONE-BYTES-EXACT; I-CODE-IDENTITY-LINKAGE; I-IMPL-NONVACUOUS; I-DIRECT-IMPL-CALL-INERT; I-DEPLOY-INIT-ATOMIC
criteria.statement: Zero immutable slots; the clone is byte-exactly template + implementation + 48 args; the bare implementation cannot be initialised and holds no authority; deployment and initialisation are atomic.
criteria.measuredReason: Byte figures exist; the offline identity chain was never executed for the plane.

criteria.statement: One immutable factory per generation binding implementation, generation, root and asset at construction; no setter; the salt binds the complete genesis authority.

The real checker classifies every external state-changing function of the candidate under a Generation-2 manifest, with the mechanism reached before the first effect; a derived comparison with Generation 1 shows NO_NEW_PRIVILEGED_PRINCIPAL; the ERC-20 external call is modelled as a new effect surface.
criteria.measuredReason: #237 reused the Generation-1 manifest; no Generation-2 census artifact exists and no call census exists.

criteria.source: stateful/defects.ts SD-3, SD-6, SD-7; G-PQ-COMMITMENT-SATISFIABLE; G-COMMITMENT-ATTESTED
criteria.statement: No accepted transition leaves a mandatory conjunct with no possible witness; a dead vault is reachable only by the declared deliberate routes.

The campaign, extended to Generation 2, composes histories with ERC-20 state under an asymmetric oracle and with mutation adequacy: no violation unexplained by the ledger, every positive control passes, every action and outcome reached.
criteria.measuredReason: #237 records this as blocker 4: the campaign binds Generation 1.

criteria.statement: Slither at the pinned commit runs on the candidate itself and every own-code finding is adjudicated by semantic identity; CodeQL's limit is stated; no scanner result is carried from Generation 1.
criteria.measuredReason: The candidates are outside the scanner scope.

criteria.statement: Candidate identity is reconstructible from committed source; every receipt names its subject, never its container; currency is licensed by byte equality of the measured inputs; no timestamp or machine path enters the identity.
criteria.measuredReason: #237 pins source hashes in a measurement record, not an admission identity.

criteria.source: architecture 19.0 and 19.2 STOP CONDITION; H-20; SG-01
criteria.statement: Final runtime at or below TARGET_KERNEL_CEILING with at least 600 B of headroom, re-measured after every admission change, every delta from measured Variant A published; zero immutable slots.
criteria.measuredReason: 18,572 B, headroom 3,404, 2,804 above the stop line, measured in #237.

criteria.statement: Asset fixed at Vault creation.
No setter exists, on the kernel or the factory, proven from the ABI and from the AST (no storage word holds the asset).
A caller cannot select the asset, including by appended calldata.
criteria.measuredReason: No mutant establishes the property has teeth.

criteria.source: owner lane requirement 5; relayer threat model
criteria.statement: A relayer cannot select the asset.
The credential cannot mutate the asset in place across any history.
A guardian quorum cannot mutate the asset in place, recovery included.
WalletWall owns no asset-selection authority; the only choice is the factory's constructor argument, spent at construction (H-32 discovery residual).
Changing the asset requires migration to a new Vault; the vault's asset read never changes.
A different admitted asset changes the Vault's address, code and therefore its signing domain.
A signature for one asset's vault fails at the other's, both ways, over histories, with the same credential on both.

Spend settlement requires the observed exact decrease; the boolean is never trusted; a failed query refuses; every refusal is atomic. What the kernel can observe is recorded apart from what the asset must guarantee.

criteria.source: owner lane requirement 12; custody 8 D-5; PG-03
criteria.statement: An asset-admission checklist exists and names every semantic the kernel cannot observe. No real token is admitted and no real address appears.
criteria.measuredReason: #237 section 8 lists behaviours; no checklist exists.

criteria.source: AUTHORITY.md section 5; KERNEL_ADMISSION section 2 (ERC-1271 not in generation 1); PG-02
criteria.statement: The vault can grant no allowance and answers no ERC-1271 query, so a token's permit or signature-transfer path cannot authorise a debit.
Verifier presence creates no WalletWall authority root.
Verifier authority cannot move assets while requirePq == false; it is not consulted at all.
Requiring a verifier at genesis makes WalletWall infrastructure no liveness dependency.
The verifier can be created permissionlessly and creation grants no privilege.
Later verifier transitions still satisfy the existing cuts and the provenance rule.
criteria.measuredReason: No Generation-2 run against the real root.

criteria.statement: A malicious or always-true verifier stays bounded by the existing authority model.
Verifier loss cannot trap permitted migration or egress.
The candidate does not inherit the trusted-attestor problem as a hard dependency.

criteria.source: owner lane requirement 11; AUTHORITY.md section 6; PG-06
criteria.statement: A reentrant token cannot double-spend, replay, alter migration disposition, escape safe-state restrictions, exploit nonce ordering or manipulate the settlement observation; failure is atomic; state ordering carries the argument and any guard would be a measured delta.

SD-4 and SD-8 (sustained) and SD-11A and SD-11B (conditionally remediated) are each re-executed on the candidate and answered: preserved, worsened, reachable through ERC-20 paths, or accidentally fixed.
Fork-conditional code immutability is a claim about a network; identity-type separation and assurance non-actuation belong to an observatory the prototype does not contain.
criteria.measuredReason: OBSERVATORY by architecture 16.1: no assurance here. Recorded so absence is not read as coverage.

criteria.source: architecture section 6 I-VETO-BOUND (T0): 'a pending migration binding (deadline)'; section 6 transitions (any -> MIGRATION_ONLY: delayed, reversible); 13.1 Phase 1; section 16 T0 scope: 'the absence of any unbounded terminal veto'; H-10 Containment
criteria.statement: A pending binding vetoes spending, rotation, recovery, containment and rebinding, so it carries a bound that lifts with no principal acting.
criteria.measuredReason: MEASURED: no binding has a deadline and nothing ever lifts one. With egress blocked, ten years on the vault is MIGRATION_ONLY with every other capability refused. Generation 1 has the same shape, and no ledger entry records it.

criteria.concern: a binding the kernel can see would strand the vault
criteria.source: I-MIGRATION-NONTRAP (T0); architecture 13.5: 're-checked at EXECUTION, not only at preparation'; H-10 Prevention; I-VETO-BOUND
criteria.statement: A binding the kernel can see would strand the vault is refused at binding: a destination with no code, the vault itself, or a hash the destination's code does not have. What it cannot see at binding, a destination or token that later refuses what it is sent, is K-12-VETO's: that wait has no bound.
criteria.measuredReason: MEASURED: bindMigration accepts any non-zero hash and egress compares it, so one wrong hash signed at k+1 leaves egress, spending, recovery and rebinding refused forever. A vault bound to itself and a funded empty address that is deployed to afterwards reach the same state. Generation 1 has the same code, and no ledger entry records it.

criteria.source: I-MIGRATION-NONTRAP (T0) head sentence: 'an asset state with no authorized exit'; architecture 13.1 Phase 3: 'what makes ERC-721 and ERC-1155 workable'; H-25: 'ERC-20 and NFT custody arrive for free'; custody 7.1: 'Anything else that lands on the clone is reachable only by migration egress'
criteria.statement: An unsolicited holding of any class is egressable on the same permissionless terms as any other.
criteria.measuredReason: MEASURED: egress has one call shape, transfer(address,uint256), on all three kernels, so an ERC-721 or ERC-1155 holding has no exit. The kernel's documents record the fixed selectors and do not record this consequence.
criteria.addedAfterRegistration: Re-reading the invariant while adjudicating the review's finding about residual clauses.

criteria.statement: Migration neither shortens nor lengthens the maturity of any pending obligation: containment expiry and recovery delay. This kernel has no queue.
criteria.measuredReason: No criterion named it at registration.
criteria.addedAfterRegistration: A mechanical scan of every named invariant, now a test in test/Gen2AdmissionMatrix.test.ts.

criteria.statement: Credential and guardian generations only rise, and a signature under a past generation is refused.
criteria.measuredReason: MEASURED: a binding's digest names the guardian generation only, so its credential leg survives a rotation back to the same key: rotated A to B to A, a signature from two generations ago still binds.
criteria.addedAfterRegistration: The same scan, corrected by the second fresh-context review, which measured the binding's credential leg.

criteria.source: architecture section 6 I-NO-INGRESS-WITHOUT-EGRESS (T1), scope corrected to accounted paths
criteria.statement: The kernel credits no balance anywhere, so no state can book an inflow it refuses to pay out.
criteria.measuredReason: No criterion named it at registration.

criteria.concern: named invariants a kernel cannot carry, or that no longer stand
criteria.source: I-SYNCHRONY and I-PARITY (T2, a control plane this prototype does not have); I-DISJUNCTION-TAKES-MIN (a reference-model aggregation rule); I-STRONGER (architecture section 9: not adopted); I-FLOOR-SHAPE-IMMUTABLE (KERNEL_ADMISSION: retired); I-DECLARATION-SUBORDINATE-TO-LIVE-RECOVERY (AUTHORITY.md: does not exist in any Solidity file)
criteria.statement: Each is named in the normative documents and has no kernel subject. Recorded so absence is not read as coverage.

criteria.source: H-10 Prevention (T1): 'credential commitment, guardian commitment, policy commitment, expected safe state, chain id, nonce, deadline'; architecture 13.1 Phase 1; test/helpers/vaultVNextModel.ts MigrationBinding: 'Omitting any field is a mutant'
criteria.statement: A binding's signatures commit to the source, the destination's address, code hash and generation, the credential and guardian generations, the policy plane, the safe state, the chain, the nonce and a signature deadline. Withdrawn by 13.1 and not carried: an asset set and an amount.
criteria.measuredReason: MEASURED: the digest omits the credential generation, the plane and the safe state, so a signed binding outlives changes to any of them.
criteria.addedAfterRegistration: Second fresh-context review: a T1 hazard's prevention no row covered.

criteria.source: architecture 9 I-ATTESTATION-IS-AFFIRMATIVE (T1): 'the returned word equals the ERC-1271 magic value'
criteria.statement: An ERC-1271 attestation counts only when the whole returned word is the magic value.
criteria.measuredReason: MEASURED: the kernel compares the first four bytes, so magic plus anything reaches quorum.
criteria.addedAfterRegistration: Second fresh-context review. K-6 names the invariant in its source; its registered statement does not reach this.

criteria.source: architecture section 6 Required invariants: 'No minor principal can force an irreversible terminal state. Only a completed migration ... reaches RETIRED'; section 6 transitions; 22 D2: RETIRE 'the same conjunction, after bindDelay'
criteria.statement: No minor principal can force the irreversible terminal state: it is reached by a completed migration or by the binding's own conjunction.
criteria.measuredReason: MEASURED: retire() is permissionless after the delay, on all three kernels, with no migration completed. Today it closes nothing a binding has not already closed, and the three texts disagree with each other as well.

criteria.source: H-05 Prevention (T1): 'strength is a kernel-recorded ordinal per scheme'; architecture section 12; 24.2 'Silent crypto downgrade ... refused by the partial order'; KERNEL_ADMISSION K-15: SECURITY_PROFILE_DISPOSITION = DEFERRED_TO_FUTURE_GENERATION
criteria.statement: This generation carries section 12's SecurityProfile transition rules, or an owner decision defers them again.
criteria.measuredReason: MEASURED: a flat four-field struct, the construct section 12 withdrew, as on Generation 1, whose admission deferred the rules to a future generation. This is one, and no document says whether the deferral carries over.
